name: drift-in-slow
concept: The element hangs almost still, then drifts gently upward into place over a long, unhurried span. Use it for a hero element in a calm, premium layout where nothing should feel rushed.

name: gentle-rise
concept: A quick, quiet lift with almost no travel distance, as if the element simply settles into its resting height. Good for small UI details that should not draw attention to their own motion.

name: focus-in
concept: The element starts heavily blurred and sharpens into full clarity as it fades in, like a camera racking focus. Use it when an element should feel like it is being brought into attention rather than simply appearing.

name: unhurried-reveal
concept: The plainest possible entrance, stretched over a very long, gently eased fade with no movement at all. Reach for it when an element should simply exist a moment later, without any sense of arrival.

name: hush-in
phrase: fade with a hush of scale
concept: Opacity climbs while the element grows from a barely-there 0.97 scale to full size, a scale change so small it reads as texture, not motion. Use it for cards or panels that should feel settled rather than animated.

name: drift-in-diagonal
concept: The element travels a short diagonal path from the upper left as it fades in, giving the arrival a graceful, angled quality rather than a straight line. Suits editorial layouts with off-axis composition.

name: exhale-in
concept: The element grows past full size by a hair before settling back, like a soft exhale after holding a breath. The overshoot is barely visible, giving a living, unforced quality to the arrival.

name: soft-unveil
concept: A light lift combines with a defocused-to-sharp blur, as though a veil is lifted from the element. Use it for image captions or feature callouts that deserve a refined introduction.

name: quiet-arrival
concept: The element settles down into place from just above its resting spot, at a modest, unhurried pace. A calm default for content blocks that should arrive without ceremony.

name: drift-in-left-slow
phrase: drift in from the left, slowly
concept: The element glides in from the left at an unhurried pace, covering a modest distance with a long, even ease. Use it for side panels or captions in calm, editorial interfaces.

name: drift-in-right-slow
phrase: drift in from the right, slowly
concept: The mirror of a slow left drift: the element glides in from the right at an unhurried pace. Use it to balance a left-drifting sibling or when content should arrive from the trailing edge.

name: settle-in
concept: A short rise pairs with a subtle grow from 0.98 scale, giving the sense of an element settling firmly into its spot. Good general-purpose entrance for cards and list rows.

name: veil-lift
concept: A heavy blur clears well before the fade finishes, so clarity arrives first and the last moments are pure opacity settling in. Use it for a dramatic but still quiet reveal of a focal image or headline.

name: glide-in
concept: The element travels a noticeable diagonal path from the upper left, gliding smoothly into its resting position. Suits feature panels that want a graceful, deliberate sense of movement.

name: calm-reveal
concept: Opacity barely moves for the first third of the animation, then resolves fully, giving the entrance a held-breath pause before it commits. Use it where a beat of stillness suits the moment.

name: whisper-in
concept: A tiny nudge from the left with a barely perceptible overshoot, quick and light as a whisper. Use it for small inline elements like tags or icons that should arrive without any weight.

name: hush-glide-right
concept: The mirror of a whisper: a tiny, quick nudge from the right with a faint overshoot before settling. Use it alongside its left-hand counterpart for paired inline elements.

name: muted-descent
concept: The element eases down from above with a faint overshoot past its resting point before quietly settling. Suited to dropdown-adjacent content or notices that should feel composed, not snappy.

name: drift-in-upper-right
phrase: drift in from the upper right
concept: A short diagonal drift arriving from the upper right corner, calm and direct. Use it for badges or secondary content anchored near a top-right corner.

name: drift-in-lower-left
phrase: drift in from the lower left
concept: A short diagonal drift arriving from the lower left corner, giving a grounded, upward-and-rightward sense of arrival. Use it for content anchored near a bottom-left corner.

name: poise-in
concept: The element starts very slightly larger than its final size and eases down to rest, the opposite of growing into view. Gives a composed, settling-down feeling suited to modest badges or labels.

name: linger-in
concept: The element barely changes for over half its duration, then resolves fully in the final stretch, as if it lingered before committing to appear. Reserve it for moments where patience itself is the message.

name: soften-in
concept: A whisper-light blur clears alongside a barely-there scale change, both resolving together in a quick, soft motion. Use it for tooltips or small overlays that should feel weightless.

name: hazy-in
concept: Opacity and scale finish first while a light haze of blur lingers a moment longer before clearing completely. Use it where the last hint of softness should trail behind the rest of the motion.

name: veiled-rise
concept: The blur clears well before the rise and fade finish, so the element sharpens early and spends its last moments simply settling upward. Suited to portrait or profile imagery that deserves a graceful reveal.

name: calm-descend
concept: Opacity finishes at the halfway point while the position and blur continue to settle afterward, so the element is fully visible before it finishes sharpening into place. Good for callouts that should feel present quickly but polish gently.

name: soft-arrival
concept: A short descent pairs with a light blur clearing at the same pace, both resolving together for a clean, quiet arrival from just above. A dependable everyday entrance for notices and small panels.

name: diagonal-hush
concept: A short diagonal drift from the upper left clears its blur in step with the motion, arriving hushed and composed. Use it for feature cards in a quiet, editorial grid.

name: reveal-through-haze
concept: A longer diagonal drift clears through a heavy blur, as if the element is emerging from mist over an unhurried span. Reserve it for a hero or featured image that deserves a slow, atmospheric introduction.

name: float-up-in
concept: A tiny rise and scale grow drift slightly past their resting values before easing back, giving the arrival a light, floating quality. Use it for small badges or icons that should feel weightless and alive.

name: breathe-in-view
concept: A noticeable grow from 0.95 scale pairs with a short descent, giving the arrival a slow, breath-like expansion. Use it for feature panels that should feel deliberate and full-bodied.

name: tranquil-rise
concept: A short descent and subtle grow hold nearly still before resolving in the final stretch, a held pause that gives the arrival a tranquil, unforced quality. Use it for section intros that should breathe before they land.

name: gentle-glide-left
concept: A modest slide from the left combines with a subtle grow from 0.98 scale, both easing in together at an unhurried pace. Use it for side-anchored content that should feel composed rather than snappy.

name: gentle-glide-right
concept: The mirror of a left glide: a modest slide from the right combines with a subtle grow from 0.98 scale, easing in together at an unhurried pace. Use it for right-anchored content in a balanced layout.

name: poised-arrival
concept: A small nudge from the right pairs with a slight shrink from just above full size, giving the arrival a composed, settling-in feel rather than a growing one. Suited to small labels beside body text.

name: poised-hush
concept: A short diagonal drift from the lower left pairs with a subtle grow from 0.98 scale, both resolving together for a composed corner arrival. Use it for small cards in a quiet dashboard grid.

name: dissolve-into-view
concept: The element becomes fully visible at the halfway point while a trailing blur keeps softening the edges a moment longer, as if resolving out of a dissolve. Use it for photographic content in a calm editorial spread.

name: hazed-arrival
concept: A blur and a noticeable scale grow both hold nearly still for over half the duration before resolving together, arriving as if stepping fully out of a haze only at the last moment. Use it for a slow, atmospheric section reveal.

name: graceful-ascent
concept: The element rises a noticeable distance and drifts a touch past its resting point before easing back, a graceful overshoot on a longer rise. Use it for section headers that deserve a more pronounced but still calm lift.

name: patient-fade
concept: A short descent holds nearly invisible for over half its duration before resolving fully in a late, patient finish. Use it where a beat of anticipation suits a descending element.

name: muted-rise
concept: A gentle rise and a soft blur both hold nearly still through most of the duration before resolving together at the very end. Use it for a slow, contemplative reveal of a quote or pull-text.

name: soft-settle
concept: A minimal rise and a subtle grow both hold nearly still before resolving together late in the duration, settling gently into place after a considered pause. Use it for secondary content that should feel deliberate, not eager.

name: subtle-exhale
concept: The element descends while growing from 0.97 scale, drifting a touch past its resting size and position before easing back, a quiet exhale on the way down. Use it for notification banners that should feel soft, not sudden.

name: long-exhale
concept: A heavy blur clears while the element grows past full size before settling back, an extended, more pronounced exhale than a quick one. Reserve it for a slow, atmospheric hero reveal that can afford a longer breath.

name: drift-in-and-hover
phrase: drift in and hover to rest
concept: A short diagonal drift eases slightly past its resting point before settling, as if it hovered for a moment before landing. Use it for small floating badges anchored near a corner.

name: graceful-diagonal-rise
concept: A short diagonal drift from the lower right holds nearly still before resolving late, giving the corner arrival a graceful, unhurried pause. Use it for pull quotes anchored near a corner in an editorial layout.

name: quiet-corner-arrival
concept: A short diagonal drift from the upper right pairs with a subtle grow from 0.98 scale, resolving together for a composed corner reveal. Use it for small callouts anchored near a top-right corner.

name: hush-diagonal-settle
concept: A diagonal drift and a subtle grow both hold nearly still before resolving together late in the duration, settling into a corner after a considered pause. Use it for feature cards that should feel deliberate rather than quick.

name: refined-unveil
concept: A minimal rise, a subtle grow, and a clearing blur all resolve together at once, the most layered of the quiet entrances. Reserve it for a premium feature reveal where every detail should feel considered.

name: editorial-reveal
concept: A descent, a subtle grow, and a clearing blur all hold nearly still before resolving together late in the duration, an unhurried, layered arrival fit for a magazine-style feature. Use it for the most premium content moments.
